title: The sun itself will be folded up.
subtitle: The first sign of the end
then: Ibn Kathir explains that takwir means folding one part of something into another, {idea}like folding a turban.{/idea} The sun will be rolled up and its light will go. The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever wants to see the Day of Judgement {reward}as if with his own eyes{/reward} should read this surah.
now: You plan your life around sunrise alarms and sunset dinners. {idea}The one thing you never doubt will be wrapped up like cloth.{/idea} Everything you lean on that is not Allah has an expiry.
old: Some things in life are simply permanent.
new: Even the sun will be folded away. Only Allah does not end.
try: Watch the sun rise or set today and remember it is on loan.

title: The stars will scatter and fall.
subtitle: The night sky poured out
then: Ibn Kathir says it means {trap}when they are scattered{/trap}, citing 82:2. The root of the word means to be poured out. Ubayy bin Kab described people {idea}in their marketplaces{/idea} when the sun's light goes and then the stars scatter.
now: You are in the supermarket queue, scrolling, planning the weekend. {idea}Ubayy pictured the end arriving on a normal market day.{/idea} Nothing about an ordinary day makes it safe from being the last one.
old: The end will come with lots of warning, on some dramatic day.
new: It may arrive on an ordinary day, while I am busy shopping.
try: Do one good deed today that you have been saving for a quieter time.

title: Mountains will move and be gone.
subtitle: The most solid thing turns to nothing
then: Ibn Kathir explains the mountains {trap}will not remain in their places and they will be destroyed.{/trap} Then {idea}the earth will be left as a flat, level plain.{/idea} The surah keeps listing what people thought could never move.
now: You call your job rock solid and your house your foundation. {idea}The verse moves actual rock.{/idea} It gently asks what you are standing on underneath all that.
old: My life is built on solid ground.
new: Only my bond with Allah is solid. Even mountains move.
try: Make a short dua today asking Allah to be your firm footing, by name.

title: The most precious camels, left untended.
subtitle: When the most valuable thing stops mattering
then: Ibn Kathir says the 'Ishar were {reward}the best type of camel{/reward}, especially those near giving birth. On that Day {trap}they will not be milked or tied up{/trap}, abandoned by owners for whom they used to be the most important thing.
now: Your new phone, your car with no scratches, your investment app you open ten times a day. {trap}One day you will walk past it without a glance.{/trap} Hold it now with that in mind.
old: My most valuable possession deserves my constant attention.
new: The things I guard most will be the first I forget on that Day.
try: Give away or lend one thing you are a little too attached to.

title: Wild beasts gathered, even the flies.
subtitle: No creature is forgotten
then: Ibn Kathir cites 6:38: every creature and bird are {idea}communities like you{/idea}, gathered to their Lord. Ibn Abbas said, {reward}everything will be gathered, even the flies.{/reward} Animals that fled people will crowd together with them.
now: You kick a stray cat away from the bins, or forget to feed the pet when you are busy. {idea}That animal is also part of the gathering.{/idea} How you treated it is not invisible.
old: How I treat animals does not really count.
new: Every creature is gathered by Allah, and my kindness to them is seen.
try: Do one kind thing for an animal today, even putting out water.

title: The seas set ablaze.
subtitle: Water becomes fire
then: Ibn Kathir links this to 52:6, the sea kindled. He cites Ali, who said of this verse {trap}the seas become as blazing fire.{/trap} In the account of Ubayy, {idea}the jinn rush to the sea and find it aflame.{/idea}
now: You stand on the beach at sunset feeling calm, the waves cool on your feet. {idea}Allah made it calm, and He can change it.{/idea} The calm you feel is a mercy, not a guarantee.
old: The natural world will always behave as it does today.
new: Every calm thing I enjoy is held in place by Allah's mercy.
try: Next time you drink water, pause and thank Allah that it is cool.

title: Every soul paired with its own kind.
subtitle: You will be grouped with those you resemble

row.title: its peers
sub: those who did the same deeds

then: Ibn Kathir explains {idea}every type of soul will be gathered with its peer.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ said each man will be with {reward}the people who performed the same deeds that he did{/reward}, and cited the three groups in 56:7-10.
now: Look at the five people you message most. Look at what you do together. {idea}That is a preview of your group.{/idea} You can still choose who you become like.
old: My friends do not say much about where I am headed.
new: I will be gathered with those whose deeds match mine.
try: Reach out today to one friend who makes you better, and spend some time with them.

title: The buried girl will be asked.
subtitle: The voiceless one is given a voice

row.title: the wronged
sub: asked first, in front of him

then: In the time before Islam, some {trap}buried infant girls in the dirt out of hatred of girls.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains that on the Day, the girl herself will be asked. {idea}If the one wronged is questioned, what should the wrongdoer expect?{/idea}
now: Think of the person at work or at home you could brush aside because they would never complain. {idea}Allah gives the silent ones a voice on that Day.{/idea} How you treat the powerless is on record.
old: If the person I wronged never spoke up, it is over.
new: Allah will give a voice to everyone who could not speak for themselves.
try: Make it right with one person you know you treated unfairly and who never said anything.

title: For what sin was she killed?
subtitle: A question with no answer

row.title: a path back
sub: the Prophet ﷺ gave Qays one

then: Ibn Abbas and others said she will {idea}ask, demanding restitution for her blood.{/idea} Ibn Kathir also reports that Qays bin Asim came to the Prophet ﷺ confessing he had done this before Islam, and {reward}was given a way to atone.{/reward}
now: There is something in your past you would rather never be asked about. {reward}The door Qays walked through is still open to you.{/reward} The question is coming either way, so turn back while you can.
old: What I did before is too dark to ever be forgiven.
new: Allah's question is coming, and so is a door back if I turn now.
try: Make sincere tawbah today for one specific old wrong, and do one good deed to follow it.

title: The pages you dictated, opened.
subtitle: Your record handed to you
then: Ad-Dahhak said {idea}every person will be given his paper in his right hand or in his left.{/idea} Qatadah said: O son of Adam, it is written, rolled up, then given to you. {reward}So let each look at what he himself dictated.{/reward}
now: Your phone keeps a screen-time report every week, and you avoid opening it. {idea}There is another report you are writing right now, line by line.{/idea} You are the one dictating it.
old: Most of my day is too small to be recorded.
new: I am dictating my own record, and I can choose what goes in today.
try: Before bed, look back on today and add one good line on purpose: a dua, a kindness, an apology.

title: The sky peeled back.
subtitle: Nothing left covered
then: Mujahid said {idea}it is drawn away.{/idea} As-Suddi said {trap}stripped off.{/trap} After the pages are opened, the sky itself is pulled back. {reward}The whole scene is about things being uncovered.{/reward}
now: You close the door, turn the screen away, and feel unseen. {idea}Nothing is above your head that blocks Allah's sight.{/idea} That can feel heavy, or it can feel like company.
old: There are moments when no one at all is watching.
new: Nothing is ever really hidden from Allah, in this life or the next.
try: In one private moment today, do the thing you would do if you remembered Allah sees you.

title: The Fire is stoked.
subtitle: A warning given while there is time
then: As-Suddi said {trap}it is heated.{/trap} The surah has moved from the sky to the Fire. {idea}It is described to people still alive in Makkah, who could still choose.{/idea}
now: Your car dashboard shows a warning light. You can ignore it or pull over. {idea}A warning given early is a mercy.{/idea} The verse is that light on your dashboard.
old: Talk of the Fire is meant to scare me into giving up.
new: Allah warns me early because He wants me to turn back.
try: Ask Allah tonight, in your own words, to protect you and your family from the Fire.

title: And Paradise is brought close.
subtitle: The reward brought to its people
then: Ad-Dahhak, Abu Malik, Qatadah and others said {reward}it will be brought near to its inhabitants.{/reward} Right after the Fire is stoked, {idea}Paradise is set close.{/idea} Both are real, both are ready.
now: You picture Paradise as something for the very pious, far beyond you. {reward}The verse has it moving toward its people.{/reward} Each small good thing today is a step toward meeting it.
old: Paradise feels distant and meant for better people than me.
new: Paradise will be brought near to those who reached for it.
try: Ask Allah for Paradise by name today, as specifically as you can.

title: Then each soul knows what it brought.
subtitle: The answer to every when
then: Ibn Kathir calls this {idea}the conclusive response of the previous statements.{/idea} When all of it happens, every soul will know what it has done. He cites 3:30: {reward}every person will find all the good he did, present.{/reward}
now: You pack for a trip and only at the airport realise what you forgot. {idea}On that Day you will see exactly what you packed.{/idea} The packing is happening now, in your ordinary days.
old: I will sort out my deeds properly at some later point.
new: I am packing what I will bring right now, every day.
try: Add one deed to your bag today that you would be glad to find on that Day.

title: An oath by the stars that withdraw.
subtitle: Stars that hide by day
then: Ali was asked about this and said: {idea}these are the stars that withdraw during the day and sweep across the sky at night.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ recited these verses in the Fajr prayer. {reward}The oath opens the case for the Quran.{/reward}
now: At noon in the city you cannot see one star. They have not gone anywhere. {idea}Some true things are just out of view for now.{/idea} The unseen in the Quran is like that.
old: If I cannot see something, I find it hard to believe in.
new: Many true things are simply hidden for now, like stars in daylight.
try: Step outside tonight, find one star, and remember it was there all day.

title: Stars that run their course and slip away.
subtitle: Order in their appearing and vanishing

row.title: ordered
sub: by a Lord who keeps time

then: Ali described them as stars that {idea}sweep across the sky at night{/idea} and vanish by day. The oath is made by things that keep a precise schedule. {reward}The same Lord who sets their course sends the message that follows.{/reward}
now: Your calendar app sends you the prayer time to the minute because the sky is that reliable. {idea}You trust its order every day without thinking.{/idea} The verse asks you to trust its Maker too.
old: The order in the sky is just how things work.
new: The sky's exact rhythm points to the One who set it.
try: Pray one prayer today right at its start time, matching the sky's rhythm.

title: By the night as it comes and goes.
subtitle: A word that means both arriving and leaving
then: Mujahid said it means {idea}its darkening{/idea}, and Al-Hasan said when it covers the people. Ibn Abbas said when it goes away. Ibn Kathir notes the word is used for both, and {reward}it is correct that the intent could be both of them, and Allah knows best.{/reward}
now: You sit up late with your thoughts as the house goes dark, and later watch the dark thin out at the window. {idea}Night always arrives and always leaves.{/idea} So do the heavy seasons of your life.
old: This dark stretch in my life will never lift.
new: Like the night, hard times come in and also turn away.
try: Spend two minutes tonight in the dark making dua about one thing that weighs on you.

title: By the dawn when it takes its first breath.
subtitle: Morning described as breathing
then: Ad-Dahhak said {reward}when it rises.{/reward} Qatadah said {idea}when it brightens and advances.{/idea} Right after the night oath, Allah swears by the morning, the way light seems to exhale across the sky.
now: You are awake for Fajr after a rough night, eyes heavy. Then the sky starts going grey, then blue. {reward}It feels like the day is breathing.{/reward} You can breathe with it.
old: Mornings are just the start of another tiring day.
new: Each dawn is the world breathing again by Allah's command.
try: After Fajr tomorrow, step outside or to a window and take three slow breaths as the light comes.

title: This is the word carried by a noble messenger.
subtitle: What all the oaths were for
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}this Quran is being conveyed by a noble messenger{/reward}, an honorable angel of good character, {idea}and he is Jibril.{/idea} Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and others said this. The surah turns from the Hereafter to prophethood.
now: You trust a news story more if it comes from a reliable source. {idea}The Quran's chain starts with the most reliable messenger in the heavens.{/idea} It deserves at least as much of your trust as the morning headlines.
old: The Quran is a good book, like many others.
new: The Quran came from Allah through a noble, trusted messenger.
try: Read the next few verses of this surah today, knowing who carried them down.

title: Mighty in strength, high in rank with Allah.
subtitle: The status of the one who brought it

row.title: makin
sub: high rank with the Lord of the Throne

then: Ibn Kathir links it to 53:5-6: {reward}mighty in creation, mighty in strength and mighty in actions.{/reward} With the Lord of the Throne he is makin, meaning {idea}he has high status and lofty rank with Allah.{/idea}
now: A courier with a fragile package needs strong hands and a trusted name. {idea}The Quran was given to the strongest and most trusted carrier.{/idea} Nothing in it was dropped on the way to you.
old: The message may have been weakened somewhere along the way.
new: Allah chose a mighty, trusted angel so the message would arrive whole.
try: Memorise or review one short verse today, carrying it carefully yourself.

title: Obeyed in the heavens and fully trustworthy.
subtitle: A leader among angels, faithful with the message
then: Qatadah said Jibril is {reward}from the high ranking, prestigious angels{/reward}, chosen for this message. Ibn Kathir notes it is something very great that {idea}Allah commends His angelic messenger and His human messenger{/idea} in back-to-back verses.
now: Someone at work hands you a confidential file because they trust you completely. {idea}Trustworthiness is the quality Allah praises here.{/idea} It is also the one you can practise today.
old: Being reliable is a nice extra, not central to faith.
new: Trustworthiness is a quality Allah praises in His greatest messengers.
try: Keep one promise today exactly as you said you would, even a small one.

title: Your companion is not mad.
subtitle: The man they knew all his life
then: Ash-Shabi, Abu Salih and others said {idea}this refers to Muhammad ﷺ.{/idea} The surah introduction notes the Makkans called his message the talk of a madman. {reward}Allah calls him their companion{/reward}, someone they had lived beside for years.
now: When someone close to you starts praying again, the family laughs it off: he has gone a bit extreme. {idea}Labels are easier than listening.{/idea} The verse invites you to judge the message, not the label.
old: If people call someone strange, there is probably something to it.
new: A mocking label is not an argument. I can listen for myself.
try: Next time someone is mocked for their faith around you, say one kind word about them.

title: He saw him on the clear horizon.
subtitle: An eyewitness, not a guess
then: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ saw Jibril {reward}in the form that Allah created him in, with six hundred wings{/reward}, at al-Batha in Makkah. He links it to 53:5-10, and suggests this surah came {idea}before the Night Journey{/idea}, since only the first sighting is mentioned.
now: You believe a friend who says, I saw it with my own eyes, more than someone who heard a rumour. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ was an eyewitness.{/idea} The message did not come from a hunch.
old: Revelation sounds like something a person could imagine.
new: The Prophet ﷺ saw the one who brought it, clearly, in daylight.
try: Read about the first revelation today, from a reliable seerah book or talk.

title: He did not hold back any of it.
subtitle: Not guessing, not stingy

key.label: What he did with the unseen

then: Ibn Kathir reports two confirmed recitations: he {idea}does not follow false conjecture{/idea}, and he is not stingy. Qatadah said the Prophet ﷺ {reward}did not withhold it from the people. He announced it, conveyed it, and offered it to everyone who wanted it.{/reward}
now: You learned something beautiful in a class and kept it in your notes app. {reward}The Prophet ﷺ gave away everything he was given.{/reward} Sharing good knowledge is following him.
old: What I learn about faith is mostly for me.
new: Good knowledge is meant to be passed on freely, as the Prophet ﷺ did.
try: Share one useful thing you learned about faith with one person today.

title: Not the word of an outcast devil.
subtitle: A source Shaytan could never reach
then: Ibn Kathir explains Shaytan {trap}is not able to produce it, nor is it befitting of him.{/trap} He cites 26:210-212: the devils {idea}have been removed far from hearing it.{/idea}
now: Your feed is full of voices pulling you toward anger, envy, and wasted hours. {idea}The Quran pulls the opposite way.{/idea} You can tell a source by where it leads you.
old: All spiritual voices sound roughly the same.
new: The Quran leads toward good in a way no evil whisper ever could.
try: When you notice an urge toward something harmful today, say a'udhu billah and pause.

title: So where are you going?
subtitle: A question to stop you in the hallway
then: Ibn Kathir reads it as {trap}where has your reason gone{/trap}, rejecting what is clear. Abu Bakr asked the same of a delegation who recited Musaylimah's gibberish: {idea}where have your senses gone?{/idea} Qatadah said it means away from the Book of Allah.
now: You pick up your phone to check one thing and look up forty minutes later. {idea}Where were you going?{/idea} The verse asks that about your whole life, gently but directly.
old: I am drifting a bit, but I know where I am headed.
new: I need to ask honestly where my days are taking me.
try: Ask yourself once today, out loud: where am I going with this?

title: A reminder for all the worlds.
subtitle: Not for one tribe or one time
then: Ibn Kathir explains {idea}this Quran is a reminder for all of mankind.{/idea} {reward}They are reminded by it and receive admonition from it.{/reward} The surah was first heard in Makkah, but it speaks past its first audience.
now: You read the Quran like a history book about other people. {idea}It is addressed to you, on your commute, in your kitchen.{/idea} Read one verse as a message with your name on it.
old: The Quran was mainly for the people it first came to.
new: The Quran is a reminder written for me as much as for them.
try: Read one verse today and ask: what is this telling me to do?

title: For whoever wants to walk straight.
subtitle: The desire to stand upright
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}whoever seeks guidance must adhere to this Quran, for it is his salvation and guidance.{/reward} The verse puts the wish to walk straight in human hands. {idea}Abu Jahl heard it and claimed the matter was entirely up to him.{/idea}
now: You keep saying you want to be more consistent with prayer. {idea}Wanting is the first step the verse names.{/idea} The next step is opening the Book that shows the way.
old: Wanting to be better is not worth much without results.
new: Sincerely wanting to walk straight is where guidance begins.
try: Write one sentence today about how you want to walk straighter, and keep it near you.

title: You will only will what Allah wills.
subtitle: Your choice, held inside His will
then: When the previous verse came, Abu Jahl said {trap}the matter is up to us. If we wish, we will stand straight.{/trap} Then this verse came. Ibn Kathir explains {idea}the will is not left to you all{/idea}; everything is according to the will of Allah.
now: You set a goal on New Year's and feel sure you can keep it on willpower. {idea}This verse turns that confidence into a dua.{/idea} Want it, work for it, and ask Allah to make you want it more.
old: If I just try hard enough, I will stay on track.
new: My effort is real, but I need Allah to will my steadiness.
try: Make this dua today: O Turner of hearts, keep my heart firm on Your religion.
